title: Perfect Days (2023) - There really is no other way to read it

commenti.body:
Well, that's an extremely cynical view. The first thing that rubs me wrong is the implication that there is somehow a "right" way to live and that it's somehow not this. The second is the oversimplification and dismissal of any nuance.

There are simple ways to say you didn't like a movie. This "13-year old's idea of a perfect life" comes from a man in his late 70s and one in his 50s and who is actually japanese.

A pretty inhumane point of view overall.
I dislike both of the prevalent interpretations and think that MY interpretation is really the way to read it. He's reclusive but slowly breaks through the struggle for a more optimistic tomorrow.

Hey OP, I get it that everyone has a different view and interpretation of the same movie. That’s the nature of art. 

I just want to say that I have a completely opposite view to yours. This movie is about a man (who has been through a lot even though this is implied) discovering the real meaning in life is enjoying each and every small and simple things. The tears at the end are the tears of joy for living such carefree life.

I liked the movie. I see it as a subversion. First half plays it straight and second half deconstructs it. You see how clean those toilets were, before they were even cleaned? I don't think this movie is Wim Wenders falling in love with Japanese infrastructure but rather Japan's public toilets were picked to make a point. If you were to make a movie about enjoying the small things in life even if you are doing the least prestigious of jobs you would pick a more challenging environment don't you think?
Art is always the interpretation you personally think and nothing else

Wim Wenders focuses on minute details of people's daily lives, which provides insight into their world view, their thoughts, and their goals. Perhaps his greatest success with this is *Wings of Desire*, but the execution in *Perfect Days*, particularly within the context of the uniformity and ritual often associated with older generations of Japanese.

>A solitary, juvenile life lived through hobbies

Many introverts live their lives through their hobbies. I don't know what makes this "juvenile".

>This is very much Kaufman territory. 

Charlie Kaufman? If that's what you mean I think that's very much off the mark. Kaufman's an absurdist, Wenders is on the realism side of things, with a tendency toward magical realism (especially in *Wings of Desire* and the 2 or 3 flims that came after).

>I get enjoying the small things but what are the big things in his life?

I don't understand. Why must someone have big things in their lives? Many people don't, yet their lives can be as fulfilling, as happy, as heartbroken, and as devastating as those that do. That's the beauty of Wenders to me.

The urban development project in Shibuya which was tasked with designing those public toiilets, comissioned to Wim Wenders doing some kind of project to showcase them (which would explain the toilets never looking bad, I've been to Tokyo public toilets before these were made, none were terrible, but they weren't that clean). Initially pitched to him as a short film or series of short, it was Wenders who proposed doing a feature. Recommend listening to the Team Deakins interview with Wenders where he talks about the project: https://teamdeakins.libsyn.com/wim-wenders-writer-director

fuck me then this movie has the worst politics of all time haha. this is insane wenders is soo washed you're gonna make a toilet cleaner feel good movie while contractually obligated to advertise the toilets come on mannn
I thought you liked the movie.
i did when i thought it was saying something
This wasn't a commercial, they didn't dictate him what to do, you should listen to the interview.

> I get enjoying the small things but what are the big things in his life? He is a zombie

Tell us OP: What are the big things in life and what doesn't make one a zombie? What do you think are the big things that everyone needs to live a fulfilling life?

Are you talking about having kids or earning a lot of money?

this is a movie about a director invited to a distant land to look at a collection of public toilets and ends up falling in love with the tallest structure in the city.
and he thinks up a movie involving said toilets just so he can work in shots - oh so many, many shots - of his beloved Sky Tree.
